subject: Action items: signal contract + top_k calibration plan for Reranker POC
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@olivehealth.com>, Samir Rao <samir@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Action items: signal contract + top_k calibration plan for Reranker POC

Hi Ellen / Samir —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Solid discussion — appreciate the clarity on your current candidate generation flow and the expectation to keep front-end latency under 200ms for interactive search. TL;DR action items and a proposed plan below.

Summary of what we heard
- Candidate generation: ElasticSearch + filters yields ~50 candidate docs per query (post-filter).
- Relevance oracle: relevance labels available from click logs + manual eval set (~1.5k labeled pairs).
- Constraint: client-side must not block waiting for reranker beyond 200ms; server-side can allow 300–350ms for best-effort rerank w/ streaming fallback.

Proposed technical approach (high level)
1) Signal contract: we need a compact featureset per candidate — title, body embeddings (128-d), recency score, click_rate, query-doc lexical overlap, and a small set of categorical flags. Can you confirm which fields you can supply in the CSV export?
2) Retrieval -> Rerank flow: ES returns candidates -> Redwood Ranking API (rank endpoint) returns scores and optional structured output (explain tokens + function call to surface highlight spans). We'll recommend streaming partial scores to the UI, then finalize top_k.
3) top_k calibration: start with top_k=5 for production-looking UI; run offline sweeps for k in [1,3,5,10] and evaluate NDCG@k, MRR, and click-through lift.
4) Eval harness: we’ll run an offline eval using your labeled set + a synthetic augmentation we provide.

Immediate asks (can you provide by Tue?)
- Export: a representative CSV of 1k queries with up to 50 candidates each (fields: doc_id, title, body, created_at, click_rate, click_label). Label column optional.
- Auth constraints: confirm whether the POC will use API keys behind your VPC (preferred) or a short-lived token we can exchange via OAuth. If VPC, please share IP allowlist range.

Next steps + owners
- Ellen: share CSV subset (olive-rerank-signals-v0.csv) — due Tue 2027-04-20.
- Karthik: prep Redwood rank endpoint scaffold + sample SDK snippet for your engineers.
- Marissa: design eval rubric and propose NDCG/MRR targets for acceptance.
- Kimberly (me): schedule a 2-hour joint workshop for Wed 4/21 to run through SDK auth, candidate payload size, and a live re-rank run.

Attachments: I attached a short PDF with the top_k calibration plan and an auth diagram.

If anything above looks off, flag it. Otherwise, I’ll calendar the workshop and share dial-in.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action items: signal contract + top_k calibration plan for Reranker POC

Thanks Kimberly — this is great. Quick answers inline.

- CSV export: can provide 1k queries with candidates by Tues. We’ll include doc_id, title, body_snippet (200 chars), created_at, click_rate, click_label (1/0), and a category tag. Full body is sensitive; sent body_snippet only.
- Auth: POC will run inside our VPC. We can do API keys with IP allowlist (10.4.128.0/20). For long term we prefer mutual TLS, but for POC API key + allowlist is fine.
- Latency: front-end target 200ms. We can support 350ms server-side for finalization.

A few follow-ups from our side:
1) Candidate set generation: how should we pass embeddings? Base64 vector vs JSON array? Size limits?
2) Explainability: can the reranker return per-candidate feature attributions (top contributing signals) for the UI?
3) Rate limits: we expect spikes to 350 qps in peak; curious about Redwood throttling/bursting behavior.

We’ll attach a small sample CSV to the shared drive for your team.

-Ellen
Ellen Park
Search Platform Manager — Olive Health
[Attachment: olive-rerank-sample-10q.csv]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@olivehealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action items: signal contract + top_k calibration plan for Reranker POC

Hi Ellen — thanks for the quick answers. A few technical clarifications from engineering side:

1) Embedding transport: we accept both JSON arrays (e.g., [0.001, -0.23, ...]) and base64-encoded float32 blobs. For POC I recommend JSON arrays for observability; payloads under 1MB per request to keep latency predictable. If your embeddings are 128-d, JSON is fine.

2) Candidate payload: please include a compact feature map (flat key:value) per candidate. Example payload snippet in SDK we’ll drop into the workshop:
- query_id
- candidates: [{doc_id, title, snippet, embedding, click_rate, recency_secs, category}]

3) Explainability: the Redwood rank endpoint can return a structured output block with a short attribution vector (top-3 features + score contribution) and a human-readable "why" string. That adds ~20–60ms depending on model selection; we can gate it per-call (explain=true).

4) top_k tradeoffs: offline eval we’ll compute NDCG@1/3/5/10, MRR, and delta in CTR simulated by re-weighting historical clicks. For production, streaming partial scores + optimistic display of top-1 while completing top-5 is a common pattern to meet your 200ms UI SLA.

5) Rate limits: POC Dedicated pool can handle bursty 350 qps for short windows. We’ll instrument circuit-breakers and recommend a client-side retry/backoff.

Will upload a sample SDK snippet and a rank endpoint Swagger to the Drive by EOD. Also, Kimberly — can you own scheduling the 4/21 workshop?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal SWE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
